member.name: ExpectedAnnouncementSeconds
member.para: The replay that sized the reach. Calibrated 2026-08-08 by replaying the classification over the fourteen-book corpus's own Analyze signals: every mark Probe's main scan finds today is still inside its window, and the tightest real announcement leaves 2.8 s of room ("Stalker"), most of them 5-8 s. Books whose announcements sit further out than this exist - all ten the replay could not cover are marks today's Probe does not find either, recovered by the gap machinery, which is unchanged.

What trimming it would have cost. Two corpus marks are accepted 26.2 s and 28.3 s into their windows ("Die Dritte Macht" 8:06:31, "Die Maahks" 10:11:27), which is why the Gruelfin prologue lost by the 30 s jingle window in build 280 (2026-08-09) was answered with rather than by narrowing this.

member.name: SandwichedAnnouncementSeconds
member.para: The two corpus cases. Structurally identical: "De vandrande djäknarne" chapter 2 (0.95 s pause, 2.89 s of announcement, then the 2.75 s candidate) lost the chapter outright, and "The Philosopher's Stone" chapter 11 (1.39 s, 0.98 s, then the 1.78 s candidate) cost a Re-probe recovery. Both were verified with the wprobe harness: a window opened at the earlier pause reads the announcement first try.

What each bound costs. Replaying the rule over all seventeen build-331 logs' own Analyze silence lists: 2.0 s misses that book (whose announcement runs 2.89 s), 3.0 s costs 1.19x the corpus's candidates, 3.5 s costs 1.31x and 5.0 s 1.49x. Measured again over the whole build-339 corpus run, the shipped 3.5 s came out at 1.13x rather than 1.31x - the overlap cache absorbs most promoted windows.

Why a promoted candidate is still subject to the adaptive skip (measured 2026-08-20 over the frozen build-366 logs; scratchpad\promo_cost.py, promo_sweep.py). The obvious follow-up to the Philosopher's Stone case above is to exempt a promoted candidate from , since that book tightens to 5.29 s and so drops the very 1.39 s pause this rule offers. The replay says the mechanism is real and the trade is bad. Real: the promoted pause ends at 17477.46 s and the announcement onset is at 17477.48, so the window would open 0.02 s ahead of it, where the candidate actually probed (17478.44-17480.22) opens 2.74 s past it - which is why that probe read the title "Quidditch" with no chapter word in front of it. Bad: the rule promotes 3491 pauses across the corpus and the adaptive gate drops between 1031 and 1553 of them (a bracket, not an exact count, because the threshold in force at a position depends on a walk order the descending-silence books do not take in file time). 961 of the lower bound are Die Cyber-Brutzellen alone - the book whose recorded history is that extra silence candidates bought no mark at all and cost half an hour (see ). Against that, nothing is lost today: the sub-floor sweep plus Re-probe recover chapter 11 at -141.1 dBFS, and the whole ladder costs 2 min 29 s of a 4 h corpus run.

A narrower exemption was measured rather than assumed. The cost falls off roughly linearly with the sandwich width, and this chapter's 0.98 s of speech survives every width down to 1.0 s: 3.5 s -> 1553 dropped promotions, 2.0 s -> 664, 1.5 s -> 400, 1.0 s -> 171. So an exemption gated at ~1 s would cost about 1% of the corpus's window probes rather than 10%.

Rejected even in that form (user's call, 2026-08-20), and the reason is not the count. A promoted candidate that gets probed can accept a mark, can floor the scan gate and does re-cut the overlap cache, so this is not a speed knob: it changes which windows Probe opens on eight books and would need a full corpus run to clear. What it buys is robustness on a chapter that is already found, at its correct position, by machinery built for exactly this shape. Do not reopen it without a book where the recovery ladder actually fails - and do not reach the same end by narrowing this constant, since 3.5 s is what "De vandrande djäknarne" needs.

member.name: JingleFirstMinPerHour
member.para: The two populations. The corpus books this shape targets run 20-60 jingles over 10-18 hours; the books it must not fire on have no chapter music at all and tally 0 or 1 over the whole file (see for the reading that brought the spurious ones down that far). Nothing in the corpus sits between the two.

member.name: TransientSpeechFloorSeconds
member.para: The two durations this sits midway between. Calibrated against real audio (see tools\vadprobe's sweep data): the shortest musical/vocal transient measured 0.352 s and survived raising as far as 0.70, while the shortest genuine announcement word measured 0.608 s.

member.name: AnnouncementLeadInSeconds
member.para: What bounds the window at both ends. Measured 2026-08-05 by replaying the guard over each run's own Analyze speech segments across the fourteen-book corpus. Every genuine announcement clears it with room: "Corsa nello spazio"'s 65 bare numbers sit at 3.0-3.9 s, and the corpus's twelve genuine prologue/epilogue/--custom marks range from 1.56 s ("The Forever War"'s epilogue, the tightest) to 36 s. The false positive it exists to stop - /epilogo/ matching inside Italian "riepilogo" mid-sentence - measures 0.64 s. So anything in (0.64, 1.56) is defensible, and 0.85 sits low in that window rather than midway (user's call, 2026-08-05, lowered from 1.0).

member.name: AnnouncementLeadOutSeconds
member.para: The lead-out measured on a whole bare-number book. On "Corsa nello spazio" every chapter measured 1.0-2.2 s behind its number - the tightest being chapter 20 at 0.99 s - against 0.73 s for the false epilogue. 0.30 s therefore sits well below the tightest real measurement rather than just below it (user's call, 2026-08-05, lowered from 0.5).

Why it is asked of a bare number only. A heading word is routinely run straight into its text: Gruelfin's "Zeittafel" leaves 0.16 s behind it and "I Shall Wear Midnight"'s epilogue 0.44 s, both genuine, so at this threshold the first would still be thrown away and the second only just survives. Gruelfin's is a --custom mark and exempt from the guard anyway, so the exemption now rests on the principle rather than on a surviving counter-example - do not "simplify" it away on the grounds that the data no longer forces it.

member.name: MinPlausibleSpeechCharsPerSecond
member.para: Genuine pace against smeared pace. Confirmed on real audio (Perry Rhodan "Die Dritte Macht", chapters 8 and 10, 2026-07-26): two genuine segments measured roughly 10-12 letters/second, two smeared ones roughly 0.4-1.0 - an order of magnitude apart.

member.name: MarkInsideSpeechSeconds
member.para: The failure this exists to stop. Reported by ear on "De vandrande djäknarne" (build 339, 2026-08-17): that book is a LibriVox recording which announces "Inläsning av Lars Rolander" before some chapters, and the credit-to-announcement pause is short (0.55 s at chapter 6, 0.82 s at chapter 11). The survival walk kept retreating through it - a window opening mid-credit still transcribes "av Lars Rolander, sjätte kapitlet, ...", the phrase matches inside that, and the ^ guard is satisfied by the segment-start rescue because Whisper opens a segment at the announcement - so the onset converged 1.4 s inside the credit and the marks were written into the reader's name. Their default-mode positions were already right.

Why the calibration is unusually clean. The quantity is bimodal, not distributed. Replayed over all seventeen build-339 logs' own Analyze speech segments, 441 of 443 marks measure exactly zero - every jingle mark included, since the jingle anchor lands them at the music edge ahead of the segment - and the only two non-zero values in the corpus are the two reported chapters, at 1.00 s and 1.42 s. So any threshold in (0, 1.00) separates them and there is no distribution tail to fit; 0.5 sits halfway across that empty band. The same measure on the onset rather than the mark was rejected for exactly this reason: it has a populated tail out to 0.15 s over 104 marks, mostly jingles, so a cut there would sit inside real data.

Why the guard moves a mark out instead of reverting to the default (2026-08-20, from the build-362 corpus run). Reverting was only ever as good as the default-mode position happened to be, and on that run it was not good at all. The descending-silence scan () reframed chapter 11's window on the same Swedish book: build 341 read the announcement at the head of a window (probe 23.6s@3:10:09.85 (tail, +19.4s ahead), first segment "Elfte kapitlet."), while build 362 read it at the tail of probe 22.9s@3:09:51.16, where Whisper glued word and title into one 4.0 s segment. That longer segment span overlaps the 3.36 s non-speech region behind the announcement (3:10:11.71-3:10:15.07) by 2.15 s against 's 2.0, so accepted that pause as the announcement's jingle on a book with no jingles at all, and returned its far end. Default mark 3:10:14.72 - 4.8 s past the announcement, on the first word of the chapter body - and the guard duly reverted a correct refinement onto it. The deeper defect is that smeared-phrase rescue keying on a transcript segment's span, which cannot tell "Whisper smeared the announcement across a jingle" from "Whisper glued the chapter title onto the chapter word"; correcting the guard was chosen over tightening a threshold whose margin here is 0.15 s.

What the forward correction lands on, for both firings the corpus has. Chapter 6: refined mark 1:37:18.66, 1.00 s inside the credit segment 1:37:17.66-1:37:20.00, next speech onset 1:37:20.41, mark 1:37:20.06 - identical to what reverting produced, so that chapter does not move. Chapter 11: refined mark 3:10:09.12, 1.92 s inside 3:10:07.20-3:10:09.50, next speech onset 3:10:10.27, mark 3:10:09.92 - the build-341 position the user confirmed by ear. Both corrections also hand back exactly the onset the revert produced in the runs where it was right (1:37:20.41 and 3:10:10.27), which is what makes the change safe for the isolation check: chapter 11's lead-in there is 0.77 s, below , and it passes only through the segment-start rescue - so an onset even slightly different could have dropped the chapter rather than moved it. The guard has fired on exactly these two marks and no others, in both the build-339 and build-362 corpus runs.

member.name: PreciseMarkPlateauProbesSeconds
member.para: The hole, measured. 2026-07-31 on Die Dritte Macht chapter 7 (announcement "Kapitel 7" truly at 10784.5 s, established with tools\wprobe: a window ending at 10784.60 transcribes only "[Musik]", one ending at 10784.80 catches "Kapitel"). The ordinary check answered, at 0.1 s spacing with the ggml-small model: yes at 10783.44, no from 10783.49 to 10784.04, yes again at 10784.24 and 10784.44, no from 10784.54 onward. That middle "no" run is a hole roughly 0.8 s wide sitting 0.45-1.0 s before the true onset, not the plateau's end: the gallop struck it at 10783.84, bisected between 10783.04 and 10783.84, and returned the hole's left edge, putting the mark 1.16 s early. The pre-refinement heuristic mark had been 0.04 s off, so refinement made an already-good mark worse - the only imperfect mark in a seven-book run.

The same grid on the upgrade model. ggml-large-v3-turbo is perfectly monotone with no hole at all, its last yes at 10784.64 - 0.2 s past the truth, because a bigger model reconstructs a clipped first syllable.

What the spacing and reach are calibrated to. 0.3 s spacing puts a probe inside a resumed plateau as narrow as the 0.2 s one measured there (10784.24-10784.44); 1.2 s of reach clears a hole half again as wide as the one observed. Four probes costs about 4 s per mark, ~1.5 minutes on a book with 30 chapters, against a mark that would otherwise be a second out.

member.name: PreciseMarkMinSurvivalSeconds
member.para: The probabilities by clip length. Measured on Stalker.m4b's "Zeittafel" (true onset 52.7 s, end anchor 54.19 s - the detecting window's own end, which left barely a second of the announcement inside the bracket, 2026-07-30): the same phrase came back at p=0.84 from a 6.15 s clip, p=0.54 from 4.55 s and p=0.49 from 2.95 s, and it was the 2.95 s one that failed on the run's GPU and sent the edge back 4.7 s early - past which no foothold could be confirmed and the mark was left at its (30 s early) default position. At 6 s the whole sweep from 46 s to 53.5 s is monotone across the onset, and BARDIOC.m4b's chapter 21 bisects to the same edge either way.
Why not larger. At 8 s the same Stalker probe from 48.04 s came back "[Musik]" where the unextended 6.15 s window had read "Zeittafel" cleanly.

member.name: PreciseMarkMaxBracketSeconds
member.para: The segment timestamped later than its words. Chapter 21 of BARDIOC.m4b was announced at 12:26:33.4 and its segment timestamped 12:26:38.6 (2026-07-30, a 5.2 s lag), putting the whole bracket past the announcement so that no probe inside it could ever hear it. The mark was left where default-mode placement had put it, 1.1 s into the spoken announcement.

member.name: WhisperChunkSeconds
member.para: The first Gruelfin loss. Its prologue (2026-07-30): the identical decode starting at 0:03:16.18 yields "Prolog. Die Jahre des Versteckspiels..." at 17.5 s and at 23.5 s, and at 30.0 s and 50.0 s yields the narration alone with the word gone. It was a 50 s window that probed it live, because --max-jingle-length auto had not yet seen a jingle to narrow the window with, and the prologue was simply never heard.

The second, and where the cliff really is. Re-measured on the live build-280 decode at 0:03:20.19 with ggml-small (2026-08-09): read at 22.0, 23.5 and 25.0 s, gone at 27.0 and 30.0 s. So the cliff is between 25 and 27 s and not at 30. This window also transcribes identically on the GTX 1070 and the Radeon 890M, word for word and timestamp for timestamp, which is rare enough (see the project notes on cross-machine reproducibility) to be worth stating - it makes this one window A/B-able across boxes.

member.name: VerifyRereadAttempts
member.para: The framing sweep. Chapter 1 of "De vandrande djaeknarne", ggml-small, window length 21.70 s (2026-08-17, the second test machine): window starts 23.915 / 23.920 / 23.925 s read "1. Kapitlet - Gaknupptag" / "- Gjaknupptag" / "- Jacknupptag", and 23.930 - production's own offset - reads "1. Jaknuktag" with the chapter word gone. Twenty-one starts over 23.80-24.20 at 20 ms steps: 10 recover the word, flipping every 20-40 ms on identical audio at p=0.45-0.65. Ruled out by measurement rather than argument: the machine, the GPU, the thread count, the input decoder and the window length. That is where "about half" and "two or three framings take a coin-flip miss to a tenth or a quarter" come from.

The lead-in band. Tallied over the same sweep by how long the window ran before the 24.67 s announcement onset: 0.7-1.1 s recovered 0 of 3 (production sat here, at 0.74 s), 1.3-2.7 s recovered 8 of 8, 3.3-4.7 s recovered 5 of 8. Best reading of the whole sweep was a 2.07 s lead-in - "Foersta kapitlet. Jacknupptag." at p=0.97. Hence at 1.5 s, which plus a mark's own lands inside that band, and a that walks out through the next one rather than jittering inside the first.

The model ladder, at production's own failing offset. small "1. Jaknuktag" p=0.59, medium "Foersta kapitlet" p=0.72, large-v3-turbo p=0.75, large-v3 p=0.84 - monotonic in model size, and the bigger models also emit the announcement as a segment of its own instead of gluing the chapter title onto it, which is what a ^-guarded wording wants. That run's --upgrade-model was turbo, so the recognizer that gets it right was already loaded. Chapter 2 of the same book agrees: small p=0.59, medium 0.73, turbo "Andra kapitlet. Masugnen." 0.80.

What it did on a real book, first try. "Die Dritte Macht" (15 h, 35 marks all known good, build 400 vs 401, 2026-08-26): build 400 failed chapters 7, 9, 10 and 20 - four false negatives out of 35 - and went on to spend over ten minutes in gap recovery with a 50-minute trailing region still ahead of it. Build 401 confirmed all 35, and every one of the four was rescued by the first rung alone (one 24 s re-read at a 1.5 s lead, on turbo): 2:59:42.49, 3:52:24.72, 4:20:55.50 and 8:38:30.59. The whole verify phase went from 2:44 to 3:09, so the four rescues cost about 25 seconds and saved the gap recovery entirely. Wintersmith the same day is the case that needed a second rung: its chapter 10 failed the first re-read at 6:43:27.76 and was confirmed by the second at 6:43:24.26 - which is the argument against stopping the ladder at one.

What this ladder cannot fix, and why it is not asked to. Chapter 2's real failure was window planning, not recognition - every window starting in [801.70, 802.30] reads it, 12 of 12 across six lengths, and production left a 3.4 s hole with the announcement in it that nothing ever read. A reframing ladder anchored on a mark cannot reach audio outside its own window, and is not a substitute for the window planning that put the announcement out of reach.

member.name: PreciseMarkSilenceAnchorSeconds
member.para: Why the effect is per-narrator, not per-language. The plateau's late bias cost nothing on the German jingle books and broke five marks across the two English ones and the French one.

The bimodal gap distribution. Measured over the fourteen-book run of 2026-08-03 (328 refinements that reported an onset, debug logs replayed): the gap between a refined onset and the end of the silence in front of it is 0.00-0.57 s for 114 marks and 4.5 s or more for the remaining 214, with nothing at all in between - the second group being the jingle books, where music, not silence, precedes the announcement and there is no boundary to anchor to. Any threshold from 0.75 s to 4.5 s therefore produces the identical result on that corpus; 1 s sits in it with room on both sides. Not one of the 328 had its onset land before the preceding silence ended, which is what makes a backward-only correction the right shape.

member.name: PreciseMarkMusicAnchorCapSeconds
member.para: How close the VAD speech resumption normally sits. Replaying the fourteen-book corpus's own logs (2026-08-09), 116 of the 264 marks that take the no-floor branch have a jingle's speech resumption within reach of their onset, and the edge sits a median of 0.05 s behind it, 88 % within 0.10 s and none further than 0.20 s.

The two marks it is far out on. Two marks in "Gruelfin.m4b" (3:31:20 and 12:04:50) have VAD hearing speech 2.54 s and 2.65 s before the announcement; anchoring straight to that would plant both in the middle of the music. The cap buys the tail without betting on the detector.

member.name: PreciseMarkOnsetFloorDb
member.para: The levels this sits between. Room tone in a narrator's pause measured at 50-58 dB below the announcement on the two cases this was calibrated against, Paula Monti chapter 19 and The Philosopher's Stone chapter 5; the announcement's own opening consonant on Philosopher's Stone chapter 5 is the affricate of "Chapter", reaching within 27 dB of the peak in its first 10 ms. 25 dB clears both.

member.name: PreciseMarkOnsetSustainSeconds
member.para: The click that closed a silence early. silencedetect closed Paula Monti chapter 19's pause at 3:18:50.72 on a -47 dBFS mouth noise lasting 20 ms, while "Première" did not begin until 3:18:51.13 - so a rule that stopped at the silence's end alone put that mark 0.39 s early.

member.name: SequenceRestartRunLength
member.para: The corpus counts on both sides of the floor. Measured over the fourteen-book run of 2026-08-03: thirteen books produced no such rejection at all - every rejection they had was a re-detection of the chapter just accepted, equal to it rather than below it - and "The Forever War", which restarts its numbering in each of its parts, produced 27 of them in two runs of 9 and 8.

member.name: AdaptiveSilenceFloorSeconds
member.para: The two books that put the floor at 0.8 s. "Paula Monti" (2026-07-31, 4 h 34 min, French) lost five chapters to pauses of 1.39-1.49 s - that narrator's non-jingle chapter break simply sits on the 1.5 s line - and "Die Dritte Macht" (2026-07-28, 15 h 10 min) had a genuine inter-chapter silence of 0.54 s.

What an unbounded band would cost. "Die Dritte Macht"'s 0.54 s silence proposes 0.41 s, i.e. the floor, from its own chapter onwards, so the band would be the full [0.8, 1.5) over fifteen hours. The order of magnitude that implies, measured on "Stalker.m4b" (2026-07-28, 13 h 28 min): 1032 silences of >= 1.5 s against 5962 of >= 1.0 s.

member.name: SuspectGapMinMissing
member.para: Why numbers far apart are the ones that sound alike. Observed on BARDIOC.m4b (2026-07-30) where "neunzehn" (19) came back as 90, and every earlier gap on that book was one or two chapters wide.

member.name: SuspectGapReframes
member.para: The case that first demonstrated it. Chapter 13 of "I Shall Wear Midnight" came back as "CHAPTER XIII" from a 16.1 s window and as "Chapter 13" from a 48.8 s one over the same announcement (2026-07-30).

member.name: RefinedNumberVoteMinimum
member.para: How well the refinement's plurality reading agrees. Over the ten-book test run of 2026-08-01, across 271 marks it agreed with the accepted number 267 times, disagreed once - the mishearing this was built for, "Die Cyber-Brutzellen" chapter 14 announced at 7:01:30, read as 40 by the one 44 s window that found it and as 14 by all ten refinement probes - and offered nothing at all 3 times.
The four split votes, which the majority requirement is calibrated against. {18:3, 8:2}, {15:8, 510:4}, {15:11, 4:1, 5:1, 50:1}, {19:4, 9:1} - the majority was right in all four.
What a minimum of three abstains on. Measured on the same run: 4 of 271 marks, with 3 more having no numbered reading at all; the median refinement offers five readings.

member.name: MaxSequenceRepairsPerFile
member.para: How many outliers a real corpus produces. Over the ten-book run of 2026-08-01, exactly one file produced a single outlier.

member.name: MaxUnnumberedMendsPerRegion
member.para: How rarely this fires. Counted over the seven-book test run of 2026-07-31 (4.5-15.6 h each, "chapter phrase heard, no number readable, window produced no mark"): zero occurrences on five of them, exactly one on "I Shall Wear Midnight" ("CHAPTER X" re-hearing an already-marked chapter 10) and one on "Paula Monti" ("chapitre ban 5", the genuine chapter 25 that the run lost).

member.name: SubFloorSweepBandCount
member.para: The five pauses that set the range. On "Paula Monti" (2026-07-31, 4 h 34 min, French) every one of the five chapters Probe missed was preceded by a pause just under the floor: chapter 3 by 1.46 s, 12 by 1.49 s, 14 by 1.39 s, 16 by 1.41 s and 19 by 1.41 s.
The measured band populations. On that same file, top to bottom: 5, 6, 13, 36, 123 silences - roughly geometric growth downwards, which is why stopping 0.5 s below the floor is where the yield dies.

member.name: SubFloorSweepBudgetFraction
member.para: What a real book's bands cost. Measured on "Paula Monti", 2026-07-31: five gaps, one probe each, two for one of them - far below the budget, which only ever bites on a gap dense in short pauses.

member.name: MaxSettledWindowSkip
member.para: The run that skipped eleven hours. BARDIOC.m4b, 2026-08-08, build 257 (the build that first cut the candidate list at rather than at --min-silence-length). A single confident chapter-1 mark at 0:07:58 settled 6260 windows in one step and probing resumed at 11:13:27 - eleven hours of a fifteen-hour book skipped outright, with all 6260 also queued for the unconditional gap re-probe that any later sequence gap would trigger.

The chain-length histogram behind the cap. Counted over the fourteen-book run's debug logs in L:\Temp (builds 244-251, i.e. before the candidate list widened), 292 chains: lengths 1:126, 2:88, 3:38, 4:13, 5:5, 6:6, 7:4, 8:4, 9:1, 10:2, 11:1, 12:1, 15:1, 17:1, 23:1. A cap of 10 leaves 287 of them exactly as they were and clips five, for 28 extra probes across all fourteen books put together.

member.name: NamedMarkDedupeSeconds
member.para: Where the duplicate pairs came from. Four of them, seen on "Die Dritte Macht.m4b", 2026-07-28, and caught only by the second of the two checks.

member.name: CollidingChapterMarkSeconds
member.para: The disagreement that makes this a separate rule. "Paula Monti", 2026-07-31, -m turbo: chapter 13's announcement was read as "chapitre 12" by Probe and correctly as 13 by Scan, leaving two marks a hundredth of a second apart titled Chapitre 12 and Chapitre 13.
The heading spread it has to cover. Measured at 2.86 s on "Corsa nello spazio"'s "Epilogo / 2179 / Spazio profondo" (2026-08-06).

member.name: AutoLanguageProbabilityThreshold
member.para: The misdetection raising the bar would not have caught. "Das Mutantenkorps" resolved to English off a single 0.36 answer, which fails either bar - which is why the raise from 0.5 to 0.6 (2026-08-03) is justified by the retry being cheap rather than by this case.

member.name: AutoLanguageMinSpeechInWindowSeconds
member.para: How far the contiguous-run version wandered. Raw VAD segments are sentence-sized - 13779 of them in "Das Mutantenkorps", averaging 4 s - so a 20 s unbroken run is rare enough that the search for one walked 80 minutes away from the anchor it was supposed to sample near.

member.name: UnnumberedRetryLeadSeconds
member.para: The window starts that flipped one chapter between notations. Chapter 13 of "I Shall Wear Midnight" came out "CHAPTER XIII" from windows starting 0 s and 1.7 s before the phrase, and "Chapter 13" from one starting 4.8 s before it (measured 2026-07-30). The 48.8 s framing is the one matches.

member.name: DefaultSilenceNoiseDb
member.para: The measurement behind -35. Fourteen-book corpus of 2026-08-05, eight 20 s excerpts per book at 50 ms RMS frames: -35 sits inside every one of those books' gap between room tone and speech. The quietest sustained speech was "I Shall Wear Midnight" at -25.1 dBFS (p75 of its frames) and the loudest room tone "The Philosopher's Stone" at -50.1 (p5), so the narrowest margins the value actually had were 9.9 dB below speech and 15.1 dB above hiss - which is where and come from.

member.name: NoiseProbeExcerpts
member.para: The seek cost. Eight 20 s excerpts cost about a second of ffmpeg seeking on a 15-hour .m4b (measured 2026-08-05).

member.name: NoiseFloorHeadroomDb
member.para: The margin the noisiest master left. "The Philosopher's Stone", room tone -50.1 dBFS, left the default exactly 15.1 dB of room, so 15 is the largest value that would leave every reference book untouched. Rounded down to 14 for a full decibel of slack.

member.name: SpeechHeadroomDb
member.para: The margin the quietest speech allowed. "I Shall Wear Midnight", p75 -25.1 dBFS, allowed at most 9.9 dB; 8 is that rounded down for margin.

member.name: FidelityExcerpts
member.para: How far the measure moves within one book. 3.2x to 24.1x between excerpts of the same book (sixteen-book corpus, 2026-08-17) - which is why one excerpt says nothing and only a median over several is worth reading.

member.name: JingleLeadInSeconds
DefaultMarkLeadSeconds
member.para: The change and when. Raised from 0.25 to 0.35 on 2026-07-29 after listening to real marks.

member.name: PreJingleSpeechToleranceSeconds
member.para: How tightly the two marks this was written for hugged the silence end. Measured 2026-08-02: both blips began within 3 ms of that silence's end, so 0.5 s sits two orders of magnitude above the jitter.

member.name: JingleGlueMaxSeconds
member.para: The longest such fragment observed. Real trailing-narration fragments and mid-jingle vocals both ran up to about 1.1 s, well under the 3.0 s bar.
